title: The job died and I do not know why
symptoms: The job died. Where do I look first?
plain: VASP prints its errors to the screen log (standard output), not to OUTCAR, so the first place to look is the end of that log.
causes: VASP prints errors to standard output, not to OUTCAR. OSZICAR tells you whether the run stopped during an electronic loop or between ionic steps.
No message at all: usually the wall-time limit or running out of memory.

fixes.text: Read the end of the standard output (`tail -30 vasp.out`), then the end of OSZICAR (`tail -5 OSZICAR`), then `tail -40 OUTCAR`. Search this page for the keyword in the error text.
No message at all: check the scheduler log for the wall-time limit or an out-of-memory kill.
Before restarting, check that CONTCAR and WAVECAR are not empty.

title: Error reading WAVECAR, or a WAVECAR mismatch
messages: ERROR: the number of k-points / bands changed, WAVECAR mismatch
symptoms: "Error reading WAVECAR" or the run stops right after start-up
The number of k-points or bands changed: WAVECAR mismatch
plain: VASP tried to start from an old wavefunction file that is empty, damaged or belongs to a different setup.
causes: The previous job was killed while writing WAVECAR, or the file comes from a different build, k-mesh or spin setting (check with `ls -l WAVECAR`: 0 bytes means empty).
Reading a WAVECAR from a different setup (number of k-points or bands changed).

fixes.text: Delete the WAVECAR, or start fresh with ISTART = 0.
Restart from CONTCAR (copied to POSCAR) if the geometry is worth keeping.

title: The distance between some ions is very small
messages: The distance between some ions is very small
symptoms: Warning in standard output or OUTCAR: the distance between some ions is very small
plain: Two atoms in your POSCAR sit almost on top of each other, which usually means the file was read differently from how you meant it.
causes: Coordinates in the wrong mode (Cartesian read as Direct or vice versa), a wrong scaling factor, or duplicated atoms (for example duplicate sites from a CIF).
The atom counts on line 7 do not match the coordinates.

fixes.text: Open POSCAR in VESTA and look at it.
Check the Direct/Cartesian line and line 2 (the scale).
Check that the atom counts on line 7 match the coordinates and that a CIF did not give duplicate sites.

title: IBZKPT: reciprocal lattice and k-lattice belong to different classes
messages: VERY BAD NEWS! internal error in subroutine IBZKPT
Reciprocal lattice and k-lattice belong to different class of lattices
symptoms: VERY BAD NEWS! internal error in subroutine IBZKPT: Reciprocal lattice and k-lattice belong to different class of lattices. Appears during setup.
plain: The k-point mesh does not have the same symmetry as your cell, so VASP cannot reduce it.
causes: The k-mesh does not share the lattice's symmetry: typically a shifted Monkhorst-Pack mesh on a hexagonal or fcc cell, or unequal subdivisions on equivalent axes.

fixes.text: Switch to a Gamma-centred mesh.
Use the same subdivision along symmetry-equivalent directions.
Last resort: switch symmetry off.

title: Tetrahedron method fails with too few k-points
symptoms: Error at start-up: tetrahedron method fails for NKPT<4
plain: The tetrahedron smearing setting needs at least four distinct k-points, and your run has fewer.
causes: ISMEAR = -5 needs at least 4 irreducible k-points; large supercells or Gamma-only runs have fewer.
ISMEAR = -5 was set somewhere, for example in a copied INCAR.

fixes.text: Use Gaussian smearing as in the author's workflow.
Or increase the k-mesh if the cell is small.

title: I asked for a relaxation but the atoms fly around (temperatures in OSZICAR)
symptoms: I asked for a relaxation but OSZICAR shows temperatures (T=) and the atoms fly around
plain: VASP ran molecular dynamics instead of a relaxation because the optimizer was never chosen.
causes: NSW > 1 was set without IBRION, so IBRION defaulted to 0 (molecular dynamics). OSZICAR lines look like `1 T= 312. E= ... EK= ...`.

fixes.text: Set IBRION explicitly in every relaxation INCAR.

title: Found a more primitive cell
messages: PRICEL: found a more primitive cell
symptoms: "Found a more primitive cell" or Bravais-lattice warnings
plain: Your cell is a supercell of a smaller one. That is often what you asked for, so this is frequently only a warning.
causes: Your supercell has a smaller primitive cell, or the lattice symmetry VASP detects differs from the one you set.

fixes.text: Usually harmless for intended supercells; ignore it deliberately.
If unexpected, compare the space group in OUTCAR with the one you meant to build, or use the primitive cell.
If it breaks the run, switch symmetry off.

title: The electronic loop does not converge
symptoms: Electronic loop does not converge (NELM reached, dE oscillates or stalls)
OSZICAR: 60 DAV/RMM lines per ionic step, dE jumping by about 1E-2
plain: VASP could not settle the electron density within the allowed number of steps; the cause is often a broken structure, not the settings.
causes: Charge sloshing in metals, slabs or large cells; a poor starting guess; a magnetic state flipping between solutions; too few empty bands; an unsuitable algorithm.
A broken geometry (overlapping atoms) causes most "unconvergeable" cases.

fixes.text: Check the structure first: overlapping atoms or a broken geometry.
Use a more robust algorithm and allow more steps.
Reduce mixing (linear mixing for slabs and charge sloshing); for magnets also reduce the magnetic mixing.
Use slightly larger smearing for metals (SIGMA 0.1 to 0.2) during the hard phase.
Increase NBANDS by about 20 % when the highest bands are occupied.
Start from a converged WAVECAR of a simpler setting (for example PBE before HSE, or non-magnetic before magnetic).

title: Sub-Space-Matrix is not hermitian, or EDDDAV: call to ZHEGV failed
messages: Sub-Space-Matrix is not hermitian in DAV
symptoms: Sub-Space-Matrix is not hermitian in DAV
Error EDDDAV: Call to ZHEGV failed (error in standard output during the Davidson step)
plain: The numerical solver for the electron states broke down, most often because the structure is bad or the start was unstable.
causes: Numerical breakdown of the Davidson diagonalization, often from a bad geometry, an unstable start, or aggressive settings.
An ill-conditioned subspace, often bad geometry or a random start.

fixes.text: Check the geometry for very short interatomic distances.
Change the algorithm (for example to All, Normal or Damped).
Restart without WAVECAR: delete it or set ISTART = 0.
Try a different NCORE or fewer ranks to rule out parallel issues.

title: BRMIX: very serious problems, the old and new charge density differ
messages: BRMIX: very serious problems the old and the new charge density differ
symptoms: BRMIX: very serious problems the old and the new charge density differ
plain: The charge density VASP read or mixed does not fit the current structure, often because an old CHGCAR or WAVECAR was left in the folder.
causes: The density read or mixed is inconsistent with the current setup, often after restarting with a changed structure, cell or symmetry (CHGCAR/WAVECAR from a different structure).

fixes.text: Restart without CHGCAR and WAVECAR.
Set ISYM = 0 if symmetry changes between steps.
Reduce AMIX and BMIX if it recurs during a normal SCF.

title: Large entropy term T*S in OUTCAR
symptoms: Large "entropy T*S" in OUTCAR (`grep "EENTRO" OUTCAR | tail -1`)
plain: Your smearing width is too large for this system, so the smeared energy is far from the energy you want.
causes: SIGMA is too large for the system, so the smeared energy is far from the zero-smearing energy.

fixes.text: Reduce SIGMA until |T*S| per atom is below 1 meV (Heuristic).
For insulators use Gaussian smearing with a small SIGMA, or the tetrahedron method for static runs.

title: The relaxation does not finish, or forces oscillate just above EDIFFG
symptoms: Relaxation does not finish in NSW steps, or forces oscillate just above EDIFFG
OSZICAR energies go up and down; OUTCAR never prints "reached required accuracy"
plain: The structure optimizer keeps stepping around the minimum without settling, usually because the forces are noisy.
causes: Noisy forces from loose electronic convergence, a step size too large near the minimum, or a very flat energy surface.

fixes.text: Copy CONTCAR to POSCAR and continue.
Tighten EDIFF and set a minimum number of electronic steps.
Reduce the step size.
Switch IBRION from 2 to 1 for the final steps (or to 3 for poor starts).
For small cells use PREC = Accurate and LREAL = .FALSE.; test ADDGRID.

title: ZBRENT: fatal error in bracketing
symptoms: ZBRENT: fatal error in bracketing (error in standard output during an IBRION = 2 relaxation)
plain: The optimizer lost track of where the energy minimum is along its search direction; the structure may already be close to converged.
causes: The conjugate-gradient line search could not bracket a minimum, usually because forces are noisy or the structure is already near the minimum.
Poor forces or step.

fixes.text: Copy CONTCAR to POSCAR and restart.
Tighten EDIFF.
Switch to IBRION = 1, or reduce POTIM.
If forces are already below your target, the structure may simply be converged.

title: The lattice keeps changing when I rerun ISIF = 3 (Pulay stress)
symptoms: Lattice keeps changing when I rerun ISIF = 3, or the static energy disagrees with the relaxation
OUTCAR "external pressure" and "Pulay stress"; volume differs between successive runs
plain: The calculation's basis is tied to the starting cell, so a big change of volume gives biased stress until you restart.
causes: Pulay stress: the plane-wave basis is set up for the starting cell. As the volume changes, the effective cutoff changes and the stress is biased.

fixes.text: Use ENCUT of about 1.3 times the largest ENMAX for cell relaxations.
Rerun from CONTCAR until the volume no longer changes (normally 2 to 3 rounds).
Finish with a static run at the final structure.

title: The vacuum layer of my slab disappeared
symptoms: My slab's vacuum layer disappeared
c lattice vector shrinks in CONTCAR
plain: The cell was allowed to change shape, and empty space offers no resistance, so it was squeezed out.
causes: ISIF = 3 relaxes the cell; the vacuum has no stress to resist compression.

fixes.text: Use ISIF = 2 for slabs, surfaces and molecules in a box.

title: The magnetic moment collapses to zero
symptoms: The magnetic moment collapses to zero
OSZICAR "mag=" tends to 0.000
Moment collapses to 0
plain: The run lost its magnetism: either spin was never switched on, the starting moment was too small, or the material really is non-magnetic.
causes: ISPIN = 1 by mistake, an initial moment too small to reach the magnetic minimum, or a genuinely non-magnetic ground state.

fixes.text: Check that spin polarization is on.
Set MAGMOM somewhat above the expected value (the handbook suggests starting at 3 to 5 Bohr magnetons).
Compare the energies of the magnetic and non-magnetic solutions to see which is lower.

title: An antiferromagnetic start ends ferromagnetic
symptoms: An antiferromagnetic start ends ferromagnetic, or moments are forced equal
OUTCAR "magnetization (x)" shows equal signs on all sites
plain: The starting pattern of up and down moments was not what you meant, or the cell is too small to hold that pattern.
causes: MAGMOM does not encode the AFM pattern in POSCAR order, or the cell is too small to hold the AFM order.

fixes.text: Check the MAGMOM order against POSCAR.
Use a supercell that accommodates the ordering.
Use ISYM = 0 if you need symmetry breaking beyond the starting pattern.

title: Bands or DOS look shifted, or the gap is in the wrong place
symptoms: Bands or DOS seem shifted; the gap appears in the wrong place
Different E-fermi values in SCF and NSCF OUTCARs
plain: The energy zero was taken from a less reliable Fermi level; use the self-consistent one or the top of the valence band.
causes: The Fermi level of an ICHARG = 11 run is less reliable than the SCF value; for insulators the Fermi level can sit anywhere in the gap.

fixes.text: Shift by the E-fermi of the SCF run.
For semiconductors and insulators align E = 0 to the valence band maximum.

title: The band structure looks wrong or noisy
symptoms: The band structure looks wrong or noisy
Jagged bands, unexpected gap
plain: The band calculation probably re-converged its own density instead of reusing the self-consistent one.
causes: ICHARG = 11 missing (the density re-converged on the path), a CHGCAR from a different structure or ENCUT, or too few bands.

fixes.text: Copy CHGCAR from the SCF of the same structure and read it without updating.
Raise NBANDS to see the conduction bands.
For hybrid functionals use IBZKPT plus zero-weight path points instead.

title: Bader charges change with settings or do not make sense
symptoms: Bader charges change with settings or do not make sense
Sum of charges differs from the number of electrons; values change with grid size
plain: The valence density alone does not contain the core electrons, and a coarse grid makes the integration inaccurate.
causes: CHGCAR alone lacks the core density, and a coarse FFT grid makes integration inaccurate.

fixes.text: Write the all-electron core files and use AECCAR0 plus AECCAR2 as the reference.
Increase the fine grid (NGXF, NGYF, NGZF) until the charges converge.

title: pymatgen or ASE cannot read vasprun.xml
symptoms: pymatgen / ASE fails to read vasprun.xml
XML parse error
plain: The job did not finish, so the XML file was never closed properly.
causes: The job did not finish, so the XML was never closed.

fixes.text: Check "Elapsed time" in OUTCAR; rerun if the job did not finish.
Some parsers can read truncated files; otherwise use OUTCAR or OSZICAR.

title: The run is far slower than expected, or runs out of memory
symptoms: The run is far slower than expected, or runs out of memory
OUTCAR "LOOP:" times per electronic step; scheduler memory errors
plain: The parallel layout does not suit this job, or the job needs more memory than each core has.
causes: Unsuitable parallel layout, reciprocal-space projection in a large cell, or too many k-point groups for the memory.

fixes.text: Large cells (more than about 20 atoms): use automatic real-space projection.
Many k-points: raise KPAR (watch memory).
Few k-points, large cell: tune NCORE (try 4, 8, 16).
Out of memory: lower KPAR, use more nodes, or use vasp_gam for Gamma-only runs.
Set LWAVE and LCHARG to .FALSE. when the files are not needed.

title: EDDRMM: call to ZHEGV failed
symptoms: EDDRMM: call to ZHEGV failed
plain: The fast electronic solver failed; a slower, more careful one usually works.
causes: RMM-DIIS failed.

fixes.text: Use ALGO = Normal instead of Fast or VeryFast.

title: LAPACK: Routine ZPOTRF failed
symptoms: LAPACK: Routine ZPOTRF failed
plain: The numerical overlap matrix broke down, typically from a badly distorted structure or a damaged WAVECAR.
causes: Overlap matrix not positive definite; distorted structure or corrupt WAVECAR.

fixes.text: Delete WAVECAR.
Lower POTIM and use ALGO = Normal.
Check POSCAR.

title: Symmetry detection errors (SGRCON, inverse of rotation matrix)
messages: VERY BAD NEWS! internal error in subroutine SGRCON
inverse of rotation matrix was not found (increase SYMPREC)
symptoms: VERY BAD NEWS! internal error in subroutine SGRCON
inverse of rotation matrix was not found (increase SYMPREC)
plain: Your atom positions are slightly off the symmetric sites, so VASP's symmetry search gets confused.
causes: Symmetry detection inconsistent with the coordinates.
Positions slightly off symmetric sites.

fixes.text: Symmetrize POSCAR (for example with the standardization step of the k-path tool).
Loosen the symmetry tolerance (1E-4 to 1E-3), or use 1E-4 or larger.
Last resort: switch symmetry off.

title: Too few bands (NBANDS too small)
symptoms: TOO FEW BANDS / NBANDS too small
plain: There are not enough empty bands, so the highest band is partly filled and the result is unreliable.
causes: The top band is partially filled.

fixes.text: Increase NBANDS by 20 to 30 %.

title: Error reading item MAGMOM
symptoms: Error reading item 'MAGMOM'
plain: The number of starting moments in MAGMOM does not match the number of atoms.
causes: The count does not match NIONS.

fixes.text: Give one value per atom (3 per atom for non-collinear runs).

title: REAL_OPTLAY internal error, or RSPHER
symptoms: REAL_OPTLAY: internal error / RSPHER
plain: The real-space shortcut for the projectors failed; turning it off avoids the problem.
causes: Real-space projection problem.

fixes.text: Switch real-space projection off.

title: CNORMN: search vector ill defined
messages: WARNING: CNORMN: search vector ill defined
symptoms: WARNING: CNORMN: search vector ill defined
plain: The optimizer's step was too large, or the electronic part was not converged well enough.
causes: Ionic step too large or poor SCF.

fixes.text: Lower POTIM.
Tighten EDIFF.
Switch IBRION.

title: LEPSILON or IBRION = 7, 8 not supported with NCORE or NPAR
messages: LEPSILON / IBRION=7,8 not supported with NCORE/NPAR
symptoms: LEPSILON / IBRION=7,8 not supported with NCORE/NPAR
plain: Perturbation-theory runs cannot split the bands over cores, so the band-parallel tags must be removed.
causes: Band parallelization in DFPT.

fixes.text: Remove NCORE and NPAR from the INCAR.

title: Imaginary phonon modes
symptoms: Imaginary phonon modes
plain: Either the structure was not relaxed tightly enough, the supercell is too small, or the structure really is unstable.
causes: Loose relaxation or EDIFF, a small supercell, or a genuine instability.

fixes.text: Tighten the electronic and force convergence and add the extra grid.
Use a larger supercell (larger DIM).
If it persists, follow the eigenvector of the imaginary mode.

title: Negative or odd elastic constants
symptoms: Negative or odd elastic constants
plain: The elastic run started from a structure that still had stress, or its settings were too coarse.
causes: Residual stress, low ENCUT, a coarse k-mesh, or a wrong Voigt mapping.

fixes.text: Re-relax at the elastic ENCUT.
Use a denser k-mesh and tighter EDIFF.
Use VASPKIT task 203 for the conversion to the standard layout.
